root_causes.RC1: Client cast requirement and identity provenance existed only in prose; nothing enforced them before spend.
root_causes.RC2: Environment master never wired into video graphs; the model invented rooms (later accepted as a deviation).
root_causes.RC3: Sequential chain without a per-clip review: each clip's drift became the next clip's opening frame.
root_causes.RC4: Seedance adds music/vocal-like sound despite SFX-only prompts; the old screen could not separate it from hum.
root_causes.RC5: Key prop (the family drawing, the paper roll) not anchored to one canonical reference; repairs changed it piecemeal.
root_causes.RC6: Model limitation in long R2V clips: invented cuts, duplicates, costume and identity drift at wide scale.
root_causes.RC7: Gate records not tied to the fix contract: pins reviewed for cleanliness, not for the state the fix needs.
root_causes.RC8: Human decisions writable by automation (record() for QC; role names accepted as users; code-signed acceptances).
root_causes.RC9: MCP submit tools sit outside the firewall; discipline is the only control.
root_causes.RC10: Final QA ends at machine measurement; no human watch/listen is required before delivery or claims.
root_causes.RC11: Billing feed not reconciled into the ledger at ingest.
root_causes.RC12: No planned delivery channel for large masters; media lives only in an ephemeral container.
root_causes.RC13: No credit-balance check before a batch; the provider fails mid-batch.
root_causes.RC14: Planning images (pencil END_LOCKs) reachable as frame sources.
root_causes.RC15: Audio-locked slot arithmetic ignored in audit/splice plans.
root_causes.RC16: Readers of shared records not updated when a record format grows.
root_causes.RC17: Process-matching shell patterns match the watcher itself.
root_causes.RC18: Segmentation was validated on raw planner times, then rounded to the 24 fps frame grid without a re-check; cuts placed at zero-gap word junctions shipped 10-15 ms inside a word.
root_causes.RC19: Storyboards were picture sheets, not executable timed contracts: no panel times on the narration, no positions, facing or prop holders, and a fixed 2x2 grid whatever the clip length.
root_causes.RC20: Approvals were stored statuses written by the agent, bound to no input hashes; handoff checks compared copied state files, so they passed by construction.
root_causes.RC21: The edit chose transitions by pixel difference (dissolve every non-matching join), so dissolves covered rendered continuity breaks instead of exposing them.
root_causes.RC22: Graph shape was chosen per job by the builder, not fixed by an approved plan: the reference node carried the storyboard sheet as @image1 (39 graphs) and two first-last-frame jobs ran with no last frame.
root_causes.RC23: No terminal-record rule: reservations, executed takes and acceptance files could stay open or contradict each other, so totals and rejection counts read from the records are wrong until someone reconciles them by hand.
root_causes.RC24: Spend authorizations had no lifetime and no closing step: they stayed AUTHORIZED after the work they named was delivered.
root_causes.RC25: Episode-specific constants in production code: the paid keyframe and video paths defaulted to project/EP05.
root_causes.RC26: The public repository doubled as the evidence store, so review frames and client records were committed to it.

contributing_factors: The chat's file transfer stops at 30 MiB, so the 466 MiB master never reached the producer
The watch page offered a joined download as a convenience, and it became the delivery path
The packaging test checked that the join decodes, not that it is a file an editor imports
failed_safeguards: finish QC, which checked the master and not the rendition that was delivered
defects.rework: re-encode of the master as a progressive MP4 and a download page (no credits)
defects.corrective_action: deliver.delivery_problems checks the box layout and codecs an editor needs; the watch page no longer offers a download; a separate page rebuilds the checked file byte for byte from parts and verifies its SHA-256 before saving.
defects.status: fixed in code; the replacement file reaches the client through the producer
defects.remaining_risk: The check covers the container and codecs; a human import test in the client's editor is still the only proof for a given file.
defects.process_change: A delivery file passes `python3 -m ulac.deliver check` before it leaves; streaming packages are never offered as downloads.

append_only.rule: Entries are never edited or removed. A changed status or a correction is a new entry in 'corrections' or 'status_updates', citing the entry it amends.

RC18.chain: planner cuts placed at zero-gap junctions -> packer checks raw time only -> frame rounding moves 4 cuts into words -> blueprint 10 ms tolerance hides SEQ_025 -> 4 boundaries ship mid-word
RC18.why_introduced: The cut planner aimed at word ends, and some word ends touch the next word.
RC18.why_allowed: pack_from_cuts checked the raw time, then rounded without re-checking.
RC18.why_undetected: No later stage validated stored boundaries until the 2026-10-15 blueprint; its 10 ms tolerance still missed SEQ_025.
RC18.earlier_evidence: Re-check the shipped frame against the transcript at packing time (free).
RC18.control_now: packer re-check after rounding; 5 ms tolerance; audio ledger BOUNDARY_MID_WORD blocks.

RC19.chain: boards drawn as 2x2 sheets with template beat windows 0/3/10/13 s -> no timing or positions on panels -> prompts carry beats without timing -> the model chooses timing and blocking -> 71 of 111 beat boundaries sit inside words; positions, props and hands drift
RC19.why_introduced: The board stage was designed as a picture deliverable, not a timed specification.
RC19.why_allowed: Board QC checked drawings against the plan, not against the narration or state.
RC19.why_undetected: Nothing compared panel times with word timestamps before generation.
RC19.earlier_evidence: Panel t_in/t_out on word gaps; zones, facing and prop holders per panel.
RC19.control_now: storyboard contract (PANELS_NOT_TIMED_TO_AUDIO, PANEL_BOUNDARY_MID_WORD, CAMERA/ACTION/ZONE checks) blocks approval; REVIEW codes for facing, regions and holders.

RC20.chain: agent signs acceptances and notes -> status fields stored, no input hashes -> state files edited after signing (2026-10-12) -> approvals stay 'signed' -> chained clips start from unreviewed or changed inputs
RC20.why_introduced: Speed: the agent was both builder and approver.
RC20.why_allowed: _user() checked role words only; gates read stored statuses.
RC20.why_undetected: No check recomputed what an approval covered.
RC20.earlier_evidence: An approval that records the hashes of its inputs fails as soon as one changes.
RC20.control_now: contracts: approvals bind content hashes, states are computed, the hook refuses agent signing; a person's video_qc PASS only.

RC21.chain: join classified by pixel difference -> non-matching joins dissolved by rule -> 9 rendered breaks covered by 8-frame crossfades -> breaks shipped as soft cuts
RC21.why_introduced: LL-20 treated a dissolve as the remedy for any non-matching join.
RC21.why_allowed: No rule required a break to be resolved before choosing a transition.
RC21.why_undetected: The transition record read the EDL, which did not list the applied dissolves.
RC21.earlier_evidence: Compare rendered join frames before choosing the transition; record the applied join.
RC21.control_now: transitions.json marks masked_break from joins.json; per-join rule in assembly_audio_qc_plan.md (code change AUD-31 still open).

RC22.chain: R2V chain designed around a storyboard slot -> video.preflight required image_1 = storyboard -> 39 paid graphs told the model the sheet was 'the authoritative director-approved storyboard blueprint' -> sketch-led staging and invented coverage risk; separately V03/V04 ran FLF with the last frame unwired
RC22.why_introduced: The storyboard was treated as the shot's staging authority inside the video model, before the keyframe-first law existed.
RC22.why_allowed: No approved plan fixed the node class, the reference set or the pinned ends; preflight checked that slots were filled, not which images were allowed.
RC22.why_undetected: QC looked at the output frames; nobody audited the graphs' inputs against the law until this postmortem.
RC22.earlier_evidence: A lint over VIDEO/*.graph.json at reservation time (node class, LoadImage set, end pins).
RC22.control_now: firewall.video_reserve -> contracts.plan_match_problems: one FLF node, both ends wired to the plan's keyframe uploads, no other image, the plan's resolution and audio setting.

RC23.chain: reservation or take created -> work moved on (402, replacement, wrap-up) -> no closing record -> metrics and the cost ledger read open or contradictory records -> committed spend, rejection count and board status misstated
RC23.why_introduced: Records were written at the start of an action and only sometimes at its end.
RC23.why_allowed: Neither the freeze nor the metrics refuse an open reservation, a take without a verdict, or two records that disagree.
RC23.why_undetected: Totals were reconciled against the billing feed, not against the record lifecycle.
RC23.earlier_evidence: At freeze: every reservation released, billed or not executed; every executed take has a verdict or 'replaced by'; one acceptance status per board.
RC23.control_now: None in code. Metrics report never_submitted and duplicate billed jobs; closing V33/V67 is a person's release decision.

RC24.chain: authorization written for a scope -> work delivered -> nothing closes it -> a later job could ride on it
RC24.why_introduced: Authorizations were recorded as states, not as grants with a lifetime.
RC24.why_allowed: No code closed or expired them.
RC24.why_undetected: Nothing listed open authorizations at the end of an episode.
RC24.earlier_evidence: An end-of-episode check of FIREWALL.json and the generation authorization.
RC24.control_now: firewall.close_authorizations (restrict-only); contracts.authorize expires (48 h default, 7 days max).

RC25.chain: module constant ROOT = project/EP05 -> next episode runs ulac.prod -> reservation written to EP05's ledger
RC25.why_introduced: The tools were written during EP05 for EP05.
RC25.why_undetected: Tests exercised the firewall directly, not the module constant.
RC25.earlier_evidence: A grep for hardcoded episode paths before the next episode.
RC25.control_now: ULAC_PROJECT names the episode every time; the modules refuse without it.

RC26.chain: review sheets and records written under docs/ -> committed -> pushed to a public repository
RC26.why_introduced: docs/ was the convenient durable place, and .gitignore covered PNG/MP4/WAV but not JPEG.
RC26.why_allowed: No rule separated client material from code and process records.
RC26.why_undetected: Nobody checked the public tree for client material.
RC26.earlier_evidence: A test over git ls-files for media types.
RC26.control_now: New media ignored; a frozen baseline and a test refuse additions; removal is the owner's decision.

Until 2026-10-15 the predecessor gate accepted any video_qc PASS, so EP05's eight 'lead (picture QC)' events would have opened the next clip. It now requires a person's PASS (test_a_video_qc_pass_written_by_the_lead_or_by_nobody_does_not_open_the_chain).

Partially prevented: 'decision' was not a guarded event (the v5 delivery decision, ledger line 852, is by 'lead'); it is guarded from 2026-10-15 (test_a_decision_names_a_person_and_quotes_them). _sanctioned is still a keyword any caller can pass, and gates.sign and five other recorders accept any name (AUD-26).
